ledger.note: 11th century: Shu Zhenduo enfeoffed at Cao. 'The state was founded sometime in the 11th century BC by Shu Zhenduo of Cao (d. 1053 BC)'; capital 'Táoqiū (陶丘)' at Dingtao; 'a vassal state in China during the Zhou dynasty (1046–221 BC)'. The year is the conquest's; the page says only '11th century BC'.

487: Song exterminates Cao. 'Duke Jing of Song captured Duke Dao of Cao in 515 BC and held him prisoner until his death'; Duke Jing attacked Cao, and 'the State of Cao was exterminated in 487 BC after the capture of Duke Fei of Cao' (the table's last ruler 曹伯阳, 502–487 BC). The page does not say what became of the land; Song, the attacker, is the successor (confidence 2). Cliopatria keeps Cao to 451.

notes: Wikidata Q204077 is shared with Cliopatria's 'Cao Cao' row (197-223 CE): different entities. 'Cao' is the Zhou-era fief at Dingtao (11th century to 487 BC); 'Cao Cao' is the Han warlord's domain in the north China of the Three Kingdoms transition; they stay separate dossiers, and the Wikidata id belongs to one of them only (the id is the ancient state's on the Cao page; the Cao Cao row should carry his own id). Cliopatria rows to correct: the Cao shape is centred 70 km west of Dingtao and overlaps Puyang (Wey); the row should end 487, not 451 (480-451 belongs to Song). Not on the pages: what became of Cao's land (Song as attacker is the researcher's reading; the Song page does not mention Cao) and the rulers' full dates (the table is in Chinese with partial years: 曹缪公 760–757, 曹声公 515–510, 曹靖公 506–502, 曹伯阳 502–487), so no ruler strip. Gazetteer name needed: Dingtao (place, Heze, c. 35.07 N 115.57 E); the dossier uses gazetteer place Heze with a 35 km radius.
